opportunities.name: Charged-flay hammer
opportunities.objective: Use one deliberately charged attack after hook/flay control.
opportunities.mechanic: E passive accumulates up to 2.1 AD magic damage plus finite soul damage when Thresh has not attacked. Trinity and Titanic add physical attack packets while Bloodmail turns bonus health into AD that can support the charged E ratio. Q hook and E displacement must secure that single attack before the charge resets.
opportunities.requiredState: Farmed-income test, finite souls, full E charge and an actual attack after control.
opportunities.failure: Low attack uptime or lost lantern/active protection costs more than the one-hit gain.
opportunities.test: Measure full-charge versus immediate second attack, separating magic E and physical item packets.
opportunities.rejectedAssumption: E charged magic bonus does not inherit ordinary physical crit or armor penetration.

opportunities.name: Soul lantern spell relay
opportunities.objective: Turn finite soul AP and a spell takedown into an additional ally recovery event.
opportunities.mechanic: Each soul adds armor/AP; W shield instead uses two times finite soul stacks, without an AP ratio. Q has 0.9 AP and a hit cooldown refund; R has 1 AP damage on only the first broken wall. Cryptbloom rewards a nearby takedown, Mandate needs Q/E immobilization and Helia can use damage before W shielding.
opportunities.requiredState: Finite souls; land Q/E, hit one R wall and throw lantern before ally damage peaks.
opportunities.failure: A missed hook or unclicked lantern loses access/rescue while offensive slots delay defenses.
opportunities.test: Record Q damage/cooldown, first R wall, lantern shield and Helia/Cryptbloom healing.
opportunities.rejectedAssumption: AP buying does not increase W shield through a nonexistent AP ratio.

ruledOut.reason: R specifies remaining walls deal no damage after the first breaks and their slow duration is halved.

unknowns: E charge timer and attack reset/proc eligibility need live tests; soul stacks cannot be supplied freely.

builds.name: Charged-flay hammer
builds.summary: Use one deliberately charged attack after hook/flay control.
builds.goal: Use one deliberately charged attack after hook/flay control.

Trinity and Titanic add physical attack packets while Bloodmail turns bonus health into AD that can support the charged E ratio. Q hook and E displacement must secure that single attack before the charge resets.
testPlan: Required state: Farmed-income test, finite souls, full E charge and an actual attack after control.
Measure full-charge versus immediate second attack, separating magic E and physical item packets.

Run three trials at matched level, ranks, gold and target defenses. Repeat against a moving opponent with a fixed incoming damage pattern. Record damage packets, missed actions, resource cost and survival separately.
Keep souls, health/mana, form, item/rune stacks, transformations and game time finite and explicitly recorded. No free full ramp or infinite scaling.
failureConditions: Low attack uptime or lost lantern/active protection costs more than the one-hit gain.
The narrow damage gain does not repay lost access, survival, wave control or allied utility.
tradeoffs: Rejected assumption: E charged magic bonus does not inherit ordinary physical crit or armor penetration.
Confidence: speculative. Source-compatible reasoning is not in-game validation or proof of novelty/optimality.
buyOrder: Candidate six slots: Trinity Force, Titanic Hydra, Overlord's Bloodmail, Spirit Visage, Sterak's Gage, Plated Steelcaps. Compare two-item checkpoints before the final six-slot test; this list is not a lane shopping order.
Keep role-appropriate starters, boots and support quest/vision obligations. If the full candidate assumes farmed income, compare it separately from support income.
coverageNotes: Only Cassiopeia Q/E and Sett W have numerical adapters. Even there, these other objectives and item/rune interactions may fall outside the model.
Proc inheritance, crit, pet hits and conditional helpers remain uncertain until observed. No completed mathematical maximum is claimed.

kitEvidence.formula:
Thresh throws out his scythe, Stunning the first unit hit and Pulling them towards Thresh for [1.5] seconds. The scythe does [100 / 150 / 200 / 250 / 300 + (0.9) × AP] magic damage and also grants True Sight for the duration.

Thresh can Recast this Ability to pull himself to the enemy.

If this Ability hits, its Cooldown is reduced by [2] seconds.

Passive: Thresh's Attacks deal additional damage based on how long since he last Attacked. They deal between [(1.7) × BuffStacks({5fbfbf13})] and [(1.7) × BuffStacks({5fbfbf13}) + (0.9 / 1.2 / 1.5 / 1.8 / 2.1) × AD] magic damage.

Active: Thresh whips his chains, Pulling or Pushing enemies in the direction of the swing. Enemies hit are also Slowed by [20 / 25 / 30 / 35 / 40]% for [1] second and take [65 / 110 / 155 / 200 / 245 + (0.6) × AP] magic damage.
Thresh collects the Souls of dead enemies by walking near them. Each Soul grants him [1] Armor and [1] Ability Power.
